aldemar.headline: Cooler CPI lifts the tape — and the blockade turns kinetic
aldemar.standfirst: Wednesday delivered the print and the tape took it well: inflation cooled again, the S&P added 0.26%, the Nasdaq 0.54%, and the VIX dropped nearly 5% to 14.55. Underneath it, the war crossed a line — a US Navy helicopter put two Hellfire missiles into a Panama-flagged tanker in the Gulf of Oman for running the blockade, the first commercial vessel fired on since the ceasefire. The date that now matters more than any headline is Tuesday: the June interim deal expires 18 August, five days out.

positions.title: Nothing open — nothing to track
positions.note: The book is flat, so there is no name-specific news to filter today. The moment a position opens, its wire gets tracked here.

themes.right: blockade enforced · interim deal expires 18 Aug
themes.title: The US fires on a tanker — and the clock on the interim deal runs out Tuesday

items.html: US Navy helicopter hits the M/V Vela Nova with two Hellfire missiles in the Gulf of Oman. The Panama-flagged vessel ignored repeated warnings while running the blockade on Iranian ports; the missiles targeted the engine room and steering gear to disable rather than sink. This is enforcement escalating from interdiction to live fire on commercial shipping — the risk premium in freight and war-risk insurance reprices off exactly this.

CENTCOM's running tally: 55 vessels redirected, three disabled, two boarded. The blockade is now a functioning naval operation rather than a declaration. Roughly 9 million barrels a day normally transit the strait, so every vessel turned back is supply that has to find another route or wait.

Pakistan's foreign minister meets Iran's ambassador to restart negotiations — the June interim deal expires 18 August. This is the single most tradeable date on the board. An extension keeps the current uneasy equilibrium; a lapse with the blockade live is the path to re-escalation, and it lands inside your position horizon.

Trump: "We totally control the Strait of Hormuz. Nobody else. Only us." Iran signals it can "prolong" the war. Both sides are talking past a negotiation they claim is advancing. Tehran's demand is unchanged — end the blockade, lift sanctions — and it is the same wall the talks hit last week.

Brent probed $90 intraday; WTI closed 82.88, down 0.38%. Crude did not follow the headline higher into the close — the market is pricing enforcement it already expected, not new supply loss. That divergence between an alarming headline and a flat close is worth more than the headline itself.

themes.note: The transmission into your screens is oil → CPI → the regime call, and this week it moved. Policy tightening's tightest gate is CPI y/y, now 3.3 against the 2.5 floor — clearing by 0.8, down from 0.96 last Friday. Two more prints like this one and the regime that has framed every edition for five weeks stops qualifying. A crude spike on an 18 August lapse pushes that gate back open; a deal drops it faster. Watch the deadline, not the missiles.

world.title: Inflation cools, the Fed gets to wait, and gold keeps buying insurance anyway

items.html: CPI cools again — monthly +0.1%, the y/y rate easing for a second month. In line with expectations rather than a surprise, which is why the reaction was orderly. Traders shifted toward the Fed holding steady from a near 50-50 split the day before; the print removed a risk rather than creating an opportunity.

S&P +0.26% to 7,748, Nasdaq +0.54%, VIX −4.8% to 14.55. Tech led the recovery after Tuesday's AI-capex selling without erasing it. The VIX back under 15 is complacency territory again — cheap protection into a live geopolitical deadline is the setup worth noticing.

Gold +1.9% to 4,467 — a fourth straight advance and the strongest since Friday's jump. Rising on a cooler-inflation day alongside a rallying equity tape is the tell: this is war hedging and rate-cut positioning at once, not an inflation trade. Gold has now gone up through every kind of session this week, which is the cleanest signal on the board.

A quiet earnings week: Cisco, Coherent, Nebius and Cerebras report. The AI-infrastructure names carry the read-across from Tuesday's Alphabet repricing — whether the market keeps charging for datacenter spending or goes back to rewarding it.

positions.title: Nothing that matters on GOOG — 1 item, all filed as noise

items.html: GOOG — "Alphabet at $343 is the same classic tech bargain it always was". A valuation opinion piece written off the price, not off new information — the mirror image of Tuesday's selling and just as empty. GOOG closed 342.37, dead flat at −0.18% while the Nasdaq rose 0.54%: the stock stopped falling but did not bounce, which is the honest read on Tuesday's capex repricing. Still 0.8R open, +5.1% on entry, stop 12.0% below.

positions.note: Signal changes the thesis, the levels or the size — earnings, a regulator with teeth, M&A, a ruling with a revenue line attached. Everything else is filed as noise on purpose; a real signal survives skepticism.
